title: The Weight of What We Take

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Anyone who steals must certainly make restitution, but if they have nothing, they must be sold to pay for their theft. If the stolen animal is found alive in their possession — whether ox or donkey or sheep — they must pay back double." - Exodus 22:3b-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God takes theft seriously, but notice how His justice is calibrated to the actual harm done. If the stolen animal was still alive and recoverable, the thief paid back double — a real penalty, but a measured one. And if a thief had nothing to pay, he was not simply let off; the debt still had to be answered. Wrongdoing has weight, and God does not let us shrug it away as though it costs nothing.

Yet even here there is no cruelty. The punishment fits the crime, no more and no less. This is the fairness of God on display — He never crushes a person under a penalty greater than the offence, nor waves the offence away as if it did not matter. In a world where the powerful often escape and the weak are overpunished, God's standard is refreshingly even.

For us, the deeper truth is that sin always incurs a debt that must be paid. We cannot simply wish it away. But where we could never pay, Christ stepped in and paid in full (Col 2:14). The debt was real; the payment was real; and the freedom He gives is real. Let this both sober you about sin and fill you with gratitude for grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I take the small "borrowings" and dishonesties of daily life seriously?
How does the reality of my paid debt in Christ move my heart to gratitude?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are perfectly fair — never harsh, never careless about wrong. Thank You that Christ paid the debt I owed. Make me honest in all my dealings, small and great. Amen.
